newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice ends mixed in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice ends mixed in active trading.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended mixed in active trading on Monday with investors liquidating their positions and moving money to the stock market, traders said.
The key October contract ended at 2,300 yuan ($277) per tonne, rising 10 yuan. It opened at 2,300 and stayed at that level for the rest of the session.
December fell 159 yuan to 2,180 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 12,700 tonnes form 1,700.
Traders said that investors continued to move their funds into the more active stock market, resulting in large scale of liquidation.
The open interest of the October contract fell 1,250 lots to 1,380 lots. One lot is five tonnes.
"The more active stock market attracted individuals' money," one trader said. "Rice is not attractive given the lack of market-moving news and the gradual reduction in open interest."
Traders said that trade would be dull in the short term as most investors had lost interest in trading.
